newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty drifts at resistance, depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty drifts at resistance, depos ease.

text.p: The Polish zloty lingered a fraction below resistance at expected intervention levels in slow early Tuesday trade without strong impetus to shade higher or lower, dealers said.

They said a light currency-selling trend remained on the market, which may later on Tuesday push the zloty into battle against National Bank of Poland (NBP) interventions, if the local unit wondered far above 1.5 percent from parity.
"The 1.5 percent level should be guarded by the NBP and the zloty should trade between 1.45 to 1.55 percent, with a slight tendency for zloty gains," said Marcin Trzykowski of Pekao SA.
At 0852 the zloty was at 1.52/1.40 percent from parity, against opening's 1.55/1.45 percent and stronger than Monday's close at 1.49/1.38 percent.
It was at 3.2210/20 to the dollar, against opening's 3.2210/40 and at 1.8645/50 to the mark, against 1.8635/55.
Dealers said the forex market waited for foreign investor orders to set the tone of the market on Tuesday.
"The market seems set to return to speculating on dollar/mark moves unless some larger foreign orders materialise," Pekao's Trzykowski said.

On the money market overnight rates eased to 22.25 percent at bid from opening's 22.30/22.45 as the market continued to remain liquid despite larger outflows stemming from higher obligatory reserve, which were increased at the start of May.

"Banks created reserves for the larger outflows and short-term rates are not likely to be affected unless the central bank heavily drains the market," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz, chief dealer at PKO BP.
Tomorrow/next rates were at 22.25/22.45 percent, slighly lower at offer from 22.25/22.55.
From the start of May, obligatory reserves on zloty call deposits increased by two points to 11 percent and by one point to five percent for foreign currency deposits.
The actual cash outflow from the increased reserves has occured from the start of June, as banks pay obligatory reserves according to the previous month's levels.
